Chance, now live on Starknet. AI agents are increasingly being trusted to move money. Chance prevents agents from hallucinating with your money. Before an agent transaction executes, Chance simulates the exact action and checks it against the user’s mandate. If it does not match, it is blocked before funds move. On Starknet, Chance uses programmable escrow wallets. Agents can propose transactions, but funds only leave escrow when the proposed action satisfies the user’s mandate. Additionally, Chance will use Starknet’s privacy framework, STRK20, to keep an agent’s mandate and settlement context private, while allowing receipts to be selectively disclosed when needed. This is what Starknet enables for the agent economy: agents can act, but users keep control of the rules, the funds and what stays private. Welcome, @Chance_

Pinned: Shipping season never ends 1⃣ Starknet is becoming a real bet on post-quantum security Starknet is one of the best-positioned blockchains to become fully post-quantum secure, end to end. > Most of the underlying architecture is already post-quantum secure, with only a limited number of remaining building blocks needed to complete the transition. > StarkWare published the full roadmap to finish the job, with Starknet targeting complete post-quantum security by 2027, well before Q-Day becomes a reality. > The Starknet Post-Quantum Hub is now live, providing one public resource to track the migration, technical advancements, research, remaining challenges, and external dependencies. > A fully specification-compliant Falcon-512 account successfully executed a real transaction on Starknet Mainnet for approximately $0.06, proving that post-quantum accounts can already operate onchain today. > Starknet v0.14.3 went live on Mainnet, with the completion of the first post-quantum roadmap milestone, with BLAKE replacing Pedersen for the OS configuration hash stored in the Starknet Core Contract 2⃣ A more efficient and robust decentralization program StarkWare proposed a major update to the STRK delegation program: > Delegation would be distributed across up to 31 validators, compared with more than 130 previously > Selected validators would typically receive between 5M and 20M STRK, compared with 2M to 5M STRK during previous rounds The objective is to strengthen validator economics, concentrate delegation among highly capable operators, and create a more efficient foundation for Starknet’s decentralization. 3⃣ Starknet privacy is entering Stage 2 > Stage 1 established the foundations of Starknet’s privacy stack. Stage 2 is now focused on bringing privacy into DeFi applications and real user-facing use cases. > StarkWare open-sourced the formal verification of the STRK20 privacy pool, with more than 230 machine-checked theorems covering its core security properties. Anyone can now rebuild the project and independently verify every proof. > The STRK20 compliance layer was fully documented, allowing users, builders, and institutions to understand the model, its advantages, and its trade-offs. The Starknet Privacy SDK and Wallet API are now live, allowing any developer to permissionlessly integrate Starknet privacy into their products.
